title: Dubrovnik Prices & Realistic 2027 Budget Guide
metaDescription: Dubrovnik costs in 2027: daily budgets from €90 to €400+, hotel, food and attraction prices, what changed recently, and how to save in the Old Town.
content:
## How Much Does Dubrovnik Cost in 2027?

Dubrovnik is the most expensive destination in Croatia and prices there compete with mid-range Western European cities. The 2026 price level is the best baseline for 2027, with a realistic increase of roughly 3–6% on food, accommodation and tickets. Budget travelers should plan €100–130 per day, mid-range visitors €150–250, and luxury travelers €400 or more. All figures below are per person per day and exclude flights.

### Daily Budget by Travel Style (2027 Estimate)

| Style | Per person per day | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Budget | €100–130 | Hostel bed or simple private room, supermarket and konoba lunches, walls ticket spread across the trip |
| Mid-range | €150–250 | Hotel in Lapad or an Old Town apartment, two restaurant meals, entry fees, buses |
| Comfortable | €250–350 | Hotel near the Old Town, restaurant dinners, a day trip |
| Luxury | €400–600+ | Boutique or five-star hotel, fine dining, boat excursions |

The lower end (€70–90) is possible only with a hostel dorm, supermarket food and free beach time. It is rarely achievable in July and August.

## How Have Dubrovnik Prices Changed Recently?

The biggest visible jump is the City Walls. The adult ticket rose by €5 in January 2026 and now costs €40 in the main season, March to October. Children aged 7–18 pay €15, and children under 7 enter free. In winter (November to February) the adult ticket drops to €15, but opening hours shrink to roughly 09:00–15:00. Some third-party sites still show older €35 pricing, so confirm the figure at the official ticket shop before booking.

Other changes since the euro changeover in 2023:

- Coffee and beer prices rose more than most staples. A cappuccino is about €2.70 in side streets and up to €5 on the Stradun, the main street. A local beer is about €4.50.
- Sit-down meals inside the walls now sit at €20–45 per person. A three-course dinner with a drink in the Old Town is around €45.
- Private apartments near the Old Town start around €80 per night in shoulder season and reach €200–350 in peak July–August.
- Seasonal swings are large. Prices run 30–50% higher in July–August than in May, June or September.

Expect another modest rise in 2027. The walls ticket is the item most likely to be reviewed, so treat €40 as a floor rather than a ceiling.

## Accommodation Costs in Dubrovnik

Accommodation is the largest single cost and the one location changes most.

### Old Town and Ploče
A private room in the Old Town is roughly €80 per night in June and €150 in August. Apartments immediately next to the walls reach €200–350 in peak season. Boutique Old Town hotels cost €180–350 and higher, and €300–500 per night in August. Luxury hotels such as Hotel Excelsior, Villa Orsula and Rixos typically charge €400–900 per night in summer.

### Lapad and Gruž
Mid-range hotels in Lapad cost around €120–180 per night in peak season and €60–90 in low season. Budget private rooms (sobe) run €50–80 in much of Croatia, and the Lapad and Gruž districts are where those rates are most realistic in Dubrovnik. Lapad is about 3–4 km from the Old Town and linked by frequent buses. Gruž is the ferry and bus port, with a daily market and cheaper konobas.

### Hostels
Hostel beds average about €36 per night across the year. Expect more in July and August.

**Opinion:** For most visitors, staying in Lapad and taking the bus into town is the best value. The €40–80 nightly saving pays for a very good dinner.

## Food and Drink Prices

| Item | Typical price |
|---|---|
| Supermarket daily food | €15–25 |
| Konoba daily menu (ručak), outside walls | €12–18 with a drink |
| Side-street konoba dinner | €18–28 per person |
| Old Town sit-down meal | €20–45 per person |
| Mid-range meal for two | about €42 (outside the busiest areas) |
| Waterfront fish and wine for two | €100–160 |
| Fine dining | €130+ per person |
| Hotel breakfast | €10–20 |

Self-catering from the Konzum supermarket near Pile Gate or from the Gruž market cuts costs sharply. Skip hotel breakfast, which is often overpriced compared with a bakery pastry and coffee.

**Insider tip:** Lunch is cheaper than dinner almost everywhere. Konobas outside the walls serve a fixed-price daily menu at lunchtime, which is the cheapest cooked meal in the city. Black risotto (crni rižot) and peka (meat or octopus slow-cooked under an iron bell, often needing pre-order) are the dishes worth paying for.

## Attractions and Activity Costs

- **City Walls:** €40 adult in season (March–October), €15 in winter. The circuit is about 1,940 m and takes 1.5–2 hours. The ticket includes Fort Lovrijenac. In summer the walls open at 8:00 and close at about 19:30.
- **Dubrovnik Pass:** The 1-day pass is priced at or close to the walls ticket, and it adds museums such as the Rector's Palace and free city buses. Prices differ between sellers, so compare the official shop first. The Mount Srđ cable car and the Lokrum boat (about €26) are not part of the standard pass.
- **Elaphiti Islands day boat:** around €80 per person in summer.
- **Cocktails:** around €10–20 each in the Old Town.

**Insider tip:** Walk the walls at 8:00 when they open. The heat is lower and the cruise-ship crowds have not yet arrived. A walls-only visit rarely beats the pass unless the museums do not interest you.

## Transport Costs

A single bus ticket is about €3.60 when bought on board, and daily passes cost around €5. Taxi tariffs start low per kilometre (under €1), but airport and Old Town transfers cost far more than the meter suggests, so agree the fare first. The Old Town is pedestrian-only, so most visitors walk. Buses from Lapad and Gruž run frequently to Pile Gate.

## Sample 2027 Budgets

### One Week, Budget Traveler
Expect €600–800 for the week on top of flights and pre-booked accommodation, which requires careful management. That assumes sobe in Lapad or Gruž, konoba lunches, and supermarket breakfasts.

### One Week, Mid-Range Traveler
A realistic figure is €900–1,200 in spending money, plus lodging if it is not already included in your per-day number. Add €120–180 per night for accommodation. For two people in a mid-range double, hotel costs alone average around €130–180 per night in season.

### Luxury, August
A boutique Old Town hotel at about €380 per night, dinner for two at a top restaurant at €150, a walls visit, a boat day at €80 and cocktails at €40 come to roughly €420–500 per person per day.

### Family of Four
A mid-range family trip needs at least €500 per day once attractions, meals and a larger apartment are counted.

## When Is the Cheapest Time to Visit?

May, June, late September and October combine good weather with lower prices. A June private room can be around €80, against €150 in August. Winter has the lowest hotel rates, with a mid-range hotel in Lapad at €60–90, and the €15 walls ticket. The trade-offs are short opening hours, and some restaurants and boat services close for the season.

## How to Save Money in Dubrovnik

1. **Eat away from the Stradun.** Prices on the main street can be double those in side alleys.
2. **Stay outside the walls.** Lapad and Gruž cut the nightly rate by roughly a third to a half.
3. **Choose the Dubrovnik Pass if you plan museums.** It can be cheaper than the walls alone once buses and museums are counted.
4. **Book peak-season rooms early.** Old Town apartments sell out first and rise the most in July–August.
5. **Use the daily lunch menu** as your main meal and buy dinner snacks from the market.
6. **Pay by card at the walls.** Most entrances are card-first, so do not rely on cash.

## Is Dubrovnik Worth the Price?

For the Old Town, the walls and the sea views, yes, but only if timing and location are chosen well. A meal in Split is often around €15 versus €20 in Dubrovnik for a comparable inexpensive meal, so travelers who mainly want beaches and food can spend less elsewhere in Croatia. Dubrovnik is best treated as a 2–3 day stop with a cheaper base in Lapad, not a two-week budget stay.

faq.question: How much does a trip to Dubrovnik cost per day in 2027?
faq.answer: Budget travelers should plan €100–130 per person per day, mid-range travelers €150–250, and luxury travelers €400 or more. These are estimates based on 2026 levels plus a modest 3–6% rise. Peak July–August adds 30–50% to accommodation.

faq.question: How much are Dubrovnik City Walls tickets?
faq.answer: The adult ticket is €40 from March to October, and children aged 7–18 pay €15. In winter (November to February) the adult price drops to €15 with shorter hours. The ticket also includes Fort Lovrijenac.

faq.question: Is Dubrovnik more expensive than Split?
faq.answer: Yes. An inexpensive meal runs about €20 in Dubrovnik versus about €15 in Split. Dubrovnik is consistently the most expensive city in Croatia, particularly for Old Town lodging and dining.

faq.question: How much does a meal cost in Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: A sit-down meal in or near the Old Town costs €20–45 per person. Side-street konobas run €18–28, and a lunchtime daily menu outside the walls costs €12–18 with a drink.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: November to February has the lowest prices, and mid-range Lapad hotels fall to €60–90 per night. For good weather with lower rates, choose May, June or September. July and August are 30–50% more expensive.

faq.question: Is the Dubrovnik Pass worth buying?
faq.answer: It is worth it if you plan to walk the walls and visit museums, since the 1-day pass costs about the same as the €40 walls ticket alone. It also includes free city buses. The cable car and Lokrum boat are not part of the standard pass.

faq.question: Where is the best area to stay in Dubrovnik on a budget?
faq.answer: Lapad and Gruž offer the lowest rates and good bus links to the Old Town, 3–4 km away for Lapad. Private rooms there start around €50–80 per night. Old Town stays typically start at €80 in shoulder season and exceed €150 in summer.

quickAnswer: Plan on €100–130 per person per day on a budget, €150–250 for mid-range and €400+ for luxury in Dubrovnik in 2027. Walls tickets are €40 in season, Old Town meals run €20–45, and July–August rates are 30–50% higher than May, June or September.
